title: Q-CTRL Unifies Boulder Opal and Fire Opal into Autonomous End-to-End Quantum Infrastructure Software - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Q-CTRL has unified its autonomous hardware characterization and calibration platform, Boulder Opal, with its error-suppressed algorithm execution software, Fire Opal, into a single end-to-end quantum infrastructure workflow. Announced on November 16, 2026, the integrated software stack automates the full lifecycle from bare quantum processor bring-up to compiled workload execution, replacing weeks of manual specialist tuning with automated routines that share real-time hardware state across calibration and compilation layers.

In conventional quantum computing deployments, bringing a newly cooled processor online requires dedicated physics teams to characterize qubits, tune individual gates, maintain drift parameters, and manually synchronize gate definitions with downstream transpilers. By linking Boulder Opal and Fire Opal over a shared hardware model, Q-CTRL enables parameter updates from autonomous recalibration to propagate immediately into circuit compilation, dynamical decoupling, and crosstalk suppression without manual database updates.

The unified stack is running live on Elevate Quantum’s Q-PAC open-architecture system in Colorado, which pairs QuantWare superconducting hardware with Qblox control electronics. End-user cloud access to the Q-PAC deployment is scheduled to open in December 2026 through Quantum Rings’ Open Quantum platform.
